title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
subject: reading

paragraphs.text: In late 1946 or early 1947, three Bedouin teenagers were tending their goats and sheep near the ancient settlement of Qumran, located on the northwest shore of the Dead Sea in what is now known as the West Bank. One of these young shepherds tossed a rock into an opening on the side of a cliff and was surprised to hear a shattering sound. He and his companions later entered the cave and stumbled across a collection of large clay jars, seven of which contained scrolls with writing on them. The teenagers took the seven scrolls to a nearby town where they were sold for a small sum to a local antiquities dealer. Word of the find spread, and Bedouins and archaeologists eventually unearthed tens of thousands of additional scroll fragments from 10 nearby caves; together they make up between 800 and 900 manuscripts. It soon became clear that this was one of the greatest archaeological discoveries ever made.

The origin of the Dead Sea Scrolls, which were written around 2,000 years ago between 150 BCE and 70 CE, is still the subject of scholarly debate even today. According to the prevailing theory, they are the work of a population that inhabited the area until Roman troops destroyed the settlement around 70 CE. The area was known as Judea at that time, and the people are thought to have belonged to a group called the Essenes, a devout Jewish sect.

The majority of the texts on the Dead Sea Scrolls are in Hebrew, with some fragments written in an ancient version of its alphabet thought to have fallen out of use in the fifth century BCE. But there are other languages as well. Some scrolls are in Aramaic, the language spoken by many inhabitants of the region from the sixth century BCE to the siege of Jerusalem in 70 CE. In addition, several texts feature translations of the Hebrew Bible into Greek.

The Dead Sea Scrolls include fragments from every book of the Old Testament of the Bible except for the Book of Esther. The only entire book of the Hebrew Bible preserved among the manuscripts from Qumran is Isaiah; this copy, dated to the first century BCE, is considered the earliest biblical manuscript still in existence. Along with biblical texts, the scrolls include documents about sectarian regulations and religious writings that do not appear in the Old Testament.

The writing on the Dead Sea Scrolls is mostly in black or occasionally red ink, and the scrolls themselves are nearly all made of either parchment (animal skin) or an early form of paper called ‘papyrus’. The only exception is the scroll numbered 3Q15, which was created out of a combination of copper and tin. Known as the Copper Scroll, this curious document features letters chiselled onto metal – perhaps, as some have theorized, to better withstand the passage of time. One of the most intriguing manuscripts from Qumran, this is a sort of ancient treasure map that lists dozens of gold and silver caches. Using an unconventional vocabulary and odd spelling, it describes 64 underground hiding places that supposedly contain riches buried for safekeeping. None of these hoards have been recovered, possibly because the Romans pillaged Judea during the first century CE. According to various hypotheses, the treasure belonged to local people, or was rescued from the Second Temple before its destruction or never existed to begin with.

Some of the Dead Sea Scrolls have been on interesting journeys. In 1948, a Syrian Orthodox archbishop known as Mar Samuel acquired four of the original seven scrolls from a Jerusalem shoemaker and part-time antiquity dealer, paying less than $100 for them. He then travelled to the United States and unsuccessfully offered them to a number of universities, including Yale. Finally, in 1954, he placed an advertisement in the business newspaper The Wall Street Journal – under the category ‘Miscellaneous Items for Sale’ – that read: ‘Biblical Manuscripts dating back to at least 200 B.C. are for sale. This would be an ideal gift to an educational or religious institution by an individual or group.’ Fortunately, Israeli archaeologist and statesman Yigael Yadin negotiated their purchase and brought the scrolls back to Jerusalem, where they remain to this day.

In 2017, researchers from the University of Haifa restored and deciphered one of the last untranslated scrolls. The university’s Eshbal Ratson and Jonathan Ben-Dov spent one year reassembling the 60 fragments that make up the scroll. Deciphered from a band of coded text on parchment, the find provides insight into the community of people who wrote it and the 364-day calendar they would have used. The scroll names celebrations that indicate shifts in seasons and details two yearly religious events known from another Dead Sea Scroll. Only one more known scroll remains untranslated.

questions.prompt: • heard a noise of breaking when one teenager threw a [1] ______
questions.explanation:
1. 全文开篇第一段第一句就提到了teenager一词；虽然第一句里并没有说到谁扔了什么，但考生只需耐心向下文再读一句，即可看到题干中noise与原文中sound的明显对应。当然，如果识别出题干中breaking与原文中shattering的同义替换就更理想了。原文中的toss一词正是用来替换题干空格前的threw，可以由此得出答案为rock。

2. 本题问的还是teenagers的举动，由此可知其定位必定与上一道题离得不远。题干问少年们走进了哪里，无论是题干中的went into，还是对应原文中的entered，都是再基础不过的词汇，对比可得答案为cave。

3. 本题定位不难，因为无论是题干还是对应原文都与上一题来自同一处，只是浅考了一下考生的基础词汇功底。题干中的containers指的是各种容器的统称，原文中的jar是其中的一种；词组made of问的是“由什么材质所构成”，对比原文中jar的材质，考生应当可以轻松得出正确答案为clay。

4. 本题的出处虽然距离上一题较远，但解答难度却不高，因为通过阅读题干本身不难看出，空格中必然需要一个首字母大写的专有名词，也就是这群人的统称。以此为线索沿上一道题定位处向后文阅读寻找，即可顺利确认答案为Essenes。

5. 本题的定位提示与上一题类似，可以根据题干上下文推知空格内需要一个大写专有名词，考生进而应该可以顺利锁定正确答案为Hebrew。

groups.instruction:
Questions 6–13

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

Choose

TRUE if the statement agrees with the information

FALSE if the statement contradicts the information

NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this

questions.prompt: The Bedouin teenagers who found the scrolls were disappointed by how little money they received for them.
questions.explanation: 判断题是一种相当考验考生能否耐心阅读、细心关注细节表达的题型。如果一个判断题型中第一题的答案是“文中未给出”，那就尤其需要考生拿出耐心来，严格遵守“一次寻找对比两道题干”的原则依次阅读正文内容，才有更大把握做对所有题目。本题就是如此。虽然依靠大写专有名词Bedouin可以快速定位到第一段第一句，但还需继续阅读几句才能看出：文中确实描述了这几个少年拿走卷轴并卖了很少一点钱，但并没有提及他们是否对这个金额感到满意或失望；而如果要彻底确认全文中真的没有说到这个信息，比较稳妥的节点是在看到下一题的对应原文时；若是追求百分之百稳妥的方法，则是在完成全文平行阅读以后（因为不排除在极少数情况下会乱序出题）。在本篇文章中，确实没有任何其他地方提到了与题干有关的内容，正确答案为NOT GIVEN。

questions.prompt: There is agreement among academics about the origin of the Dead Sea Scrolls.
questions.explanation: 题干的origin在文中原词重现，直接帮助考生定位，且定位句本身就提供了足够的信息帮助解答。无论是题干中的agreement，还是对应原文中的debate，都应该是考生认知范围中的高频常见词汇。这二者之间形成矛盾抵触的关系，因此本题答案为FALSE。

questions.prompt: Most of the books of the Bible written on the scrolls are incomplete.
questions.explanation: 大写专有名词Bible第一次出现是在第三段的结尾处，但这句话并没有说到文本的完整与否；但好在接下来的第四段第一句马上就跟进提供了足够的解题信息。考生只需认识fragments这个单词，就能轻松判定正确答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: The information on the Copper Scroll is written in an unusual way.
questions.explanation: 本题的定位倒是不难，可以直接利用大写信息Copper Scroll找到第五段的第三句话；然而仅看这句并不能得到判断答案所需的足够信息，考生需要耐心再向下多看两句，从而通过三句围绕着铜卷轴的信息综合得出正确答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: Mar Samuel was given some of the scrolls as a gift.
questions.explanation: 本题可以凭借大写人名轻松定位，原文的这一句话即可帮助考生得出结论。原文说他花了一笔钱（虽然金额不大）购买卷轴，而题干说是收到礼物（也就是不用付费），两个表述矛盾抵触，从而可得出答案为FALSE。

questions.prompt: In the early 1950s, a number of educational establishments in the US were keen to buy scrolls from Mar Samuel.
questions.explanation: 本题的定位紧随上一道题之后，这一点其实也可以从题干中的人名和数字信息中看出一点端倪。establishment一词在此处使用了一个可能略显生僻的意思，即“机构，组织”，而非抽象意义上的“建立”，但这个词义在题干上下文中应该并不难看出，所谓的educational establishment指的就是“教育机构”，对标于原文中的universities甚至是具体的耶鲁大学。原文说Samuel想将卷轴卖给这些大学却并不成功，可见大学等教育机构对此反应冷淡，这与题干信息矛盾抵触，由此可得出答案为FALSE。

questions.prompt: The scroll that was pieced together in 2017 contains information about annual occasions in the Qumran area 2,000 years ago.
questions.explanation: 本题可以直接依靠2017这个数字信息定位到最后一段的开头，但考生需要在看完此句后再耐心向后文阅读几句，才能得到足以帮助解题的信息量。原文中的364-day calendar正是在同义替换题干中的annual occasions，后一句中的celebrations...and two yearly religious events可以进一步帮助考生确认本题答案为TRUE。

questions.prompt: Academics at the University of Haifa are currently researching how to decipher the final scroll.
questions.explanation: 本题的结论虽然是相对不易确认的“原文未给出”类型，但这个结论的得出对于考生来说却不算困难。因为上一道题的出处已经将所剩的原文内容缩小至最后一段的一小部分，考生只需耐心读完全文，发现直到最后一句里文章也只是提到了“还有一部卷轴未破译”这个信息，而不知道是否有学者正在研究如何去破译它，由此可以最终确认答案为NOT GIVEN。
